gloss: to force; to compel; to coerce

definitions.gloss: to force; to compel; to coerce
definitions.explanation: To make someone do something against their will, or to impose something unwanted on someone.

examples.japanese: {無理|むり}を{強|し}いてはいけない。
examples.english: You shouldn't force someone to do the impossible.

examples.japanese: {社員|しゃいん}に{残業|ざんぎょう}を{強|し}いる{会社|かいしゃ}は{問題|もんだい}だ。
examples.english: Companies that force employees to work overtime are problematic.

examples.japanese: {住民|じゅうみん}は{長期間|ちょうきかん}にわたって{不便|ふべん}な{生活|せいかつ}を{強|し}いられた。
examples.english: The residents were forced to endure inconvenient living conditions for a long period.

notes:
GRAMMAR:
{強|し}いる is an ichidan verb despite ending in いる. The passive form {強|し}いられる is extremely common and often more natural than the active form.

PATTERNS:
- AにBを{強|し}いる (to force B on A)
- {強|し}いられる (to be forced/compelled — very common passive)
- {強|し}いて{言|い}えば (if forced to say; if I had to say — set phrase)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {犠牲|ぎせい}を{強|し}いる (to demand sacrifice)
- {我慢|がまん}を{強|し}いる (to force someone to endure)
- {負担|ふたん}を{強|し}いる (to impose a burden)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{強制|きょうせい}する is a suru-verb meaning to compel or enforce, often used for rules or systems. {強|し}いる is used more for interpersonal situations or abstract impositions.
